summary: Recent updates to Firefox's compositing and layers area focus on improving image handling and scrolling performance on Android devices. Notably, these changes implement a new method for building surface descriptors (_essential for rendering images_) and simplify how certain asynchronous methods are called, enhancing efficiency. Additionally, enhancements to the way asynchronous pan-zoom (APZ) scrolls are detected and managed ensure smoother user interactions while scrolling through content. These advancements not only improve stability and performance but also lay the groundwork for future features, reflecting a commitment to delivering a more seamless browsing experience. **This matters because effective image processing and responsive scrolling are crucial for a high-quality user experience on mobile devices.**
